statement.en:
A magic clock has numbers from 1 to 60 instead of 1 to 12. The clock has only one hand, which follows a specific rule:

- It starts at position 1.

- In each jump, the hand moves from its current position $n$ to the position $(n\times 3)$.

- If the product is greater than 60, it moves to the position equal to the remainder when divided by 60. (E.g., from 20, $20\times 3=60$, so it moves to 60; from 21, it moves to $63 \bmod 60=3$.)

How many positions (numbers) on the clock will the hand never be able to reach? (The starting position 1 counts as reached.)
